title: Intermediate versus standard dose enoxaparin to prevent venous thromboembolism in severe trauma patients: a multicenter double blind randomised controlled trial (HEPTRAUMA)
official: Intermediate versus standard dose enoxaparin to prevent venous thromboembolism in severe trauma patients: a multicenter double blind randomised controlled trial (HEPTRAUMA)
summary: Main objective: To determine the effect of intermediate versus standard dose low-molecular-weight heparin on the incidence of major venous thromboembolism following severe trauma.

interventions.name: LOVENOX 30 000 UI (300 mg)/3 ml, solution injectable

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. All adult patients (age ≥18 years) admitted to an intensive care unit following trauma with an expected stay >48 hours and a planned administration of LMWH
2. Affiliation to the French social security system or European (CEAM)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Prehospital cardiac arrest
2. History of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
3. Study drug hypersensitivity
4. Limitation of life support, life expectancy ≤7 days or palliative care
5. Contraindication to the administration of anticoagulant according to the SPC (Active clinically significant bleeding or a condition associated with a high risk of bleeding, such as a recent haemorrhagic stroke, gastrointestinal ulcer, the presence of a malignant tumour at high risk of bleeding, recent brain, spinal or ophthalmological surgery, known or suspected oesophageal varices, arteriovenous malformations, vascular aneurysms or major intrarachid or intracerebral vascular anomalies.)
6. Pregnant or breastfeeding woman
7. Inclusion in another experimental trial
8. Protected person (art. L1121-5 to L1121-8 of the CSP or art. 31 to 35 of European regulation 536/2014)
9. Hospital admission >72 hours
10. More than one dose of prophylactic anticoagulant already administered since trauma
11. Renal failure defined by creatinine clearance of 30 mL/min or less (Cockcroft-Gault formula)
12. Body weight >100 kg or <45 kg
13. Indication for therapeutic anticoagulation
14. Major known thrombophilia (e.g. antiphospholipid syndrome, antithrombin deficiency)
15. Constitutional bleeding disorder (haemophilia, von Willebrand disease, coagulation factor deficiency, platelet disorder).
16. Thrombocytopenia inferior to 50 G.L-1
